complexity.correctness_reason: Float comparison of arrival times breaks once the value cap is lifted: with target/speed around 10^16, two distinct ratios whose relative difference is below half a ulp round to the same double, so a car that should form its own fleet is wrongly merged (e.g. times (10^16+1)/10^16 vs a marginally larger nearby ratio).
complexity.notes: The print inside the loop is leftover debug output and should be removed; math.ceil is used only there and never in the logic, so the import can go too. Arrival times are compared as floats, which is exact here only because NeetCode caps values at 10^6 (distinct ratios with numerator and denominator bounded by 10^6 are always several ulps apart); replacing the division with an exact integer comparison keeps it correct for arbitrary magnitudes. Initializing result to 1 also leans on the stated n >= 1 precondition, which is fine but makes the empty case crash.
complexity.summary: Sorts cars by position, then scans from the car closest to the target backwards, keeping the current lead fleet's arrival time; a trailing car merges into the fleet if its arrival time is at most the lead's, otherwise it starts a new fleet.
